messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: `service: redis-client-connections` -> symptom: `maxclients` breach on redis-primary-0; dropped requests observed. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/redis-maxclients

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident RID-4281 created and routed to oncall. Auto-ack threshold passed, initial pager sent to alex.

alex: on it. ACKing the page and pulling metrics. seeing big spike in connected clients from inference-frontends over last 2m.

alex: quick check — redis-primary-0 maxclients=10000, current connected=10034, blocked connections increasing. 95p latency for cache get is ~600ms, error rate at ~3.7%.

jia: tagging infra — could this be a job or a client leak? I see a lot of long-lived SUBSCRIBE and CLIENT PAUSE timestamps in the logs.

alex: running `redis-cli -h redis-primary-0 info clients` now. snippet:```
connected_clients:10034
blocked_clients:142
client_longest_output_list:54000
```

maya: I'm jumping in for triage, assigning myself to mitigation. If it's client-side leak we should drop idle connections and rotate frontends.

alex: mitigation plan: 1) throttle new incoming connections via ingress temp rule, 2) force recycle long-lived clients with `CLIENT KILL TYPE normal SKIPME yes IDLE > 60000`, 3) scale redis replicas to absorb reads, 4) reduce pgbouncer/connection pool sizes towards backend to relieve Postgres pressure. executing 1 and 2 now.

ops-runner: running kill command on redis-primary-0:```
redis-cli -h redis-primary-0 --scan | xargs -I{} redis-cli -h redis-primary-0 client kill {} FILTER IDLE 60000
```

alex: applied temporary ingress rule to block 10.1.0.0/24 where a misbehaving batch job originates. Also enabled short-term connection cap at LB layer: `max-conns=2500` per frontend node.

sam: noticed similar spike correlating to a scheduled batch reindex job at 04:12 UTC — I think that job started spawning many workers that open persistent cache streams. Reindex owners paged.

maya: scaled redis replicas from 3 -> 5: `kubectl -n data scale statefulset redis-cluster --replicas=5`. Watchers: replication lag nominal. Also enabled eviction tuning for ephemeral keys to avoid tail latency.

alex: Postgres side: connections briefly spiked because of cache misses and retries. pgbouncer showed pool queueing; bumping pgbouncer pool_size from 200 -> 300 and adding short connection_lifetime. Command:```
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/pgbouncer && sed -i 's/pool_size=200/pool_size=300/' /etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini
```

jia: customer impact check: error rate on API nodes that hit cache-backed endpoints peaked at 4.1% and is now down to 0.8% after kills and scaling. 99p latency for generation endpoints peaked at 3.2s, now trending to 700ms. No active purple-level customer alerts, but some 500s logged for sandbox orgs — outreach queued.

pagerduty-bot: Incident RID-4281 acknowledged by alex at 2188887780.

maya: handing off to sam for post-incident follow-up and deeper root cause. I'll stay on for 10m to monitor. sam pls own the postmortem.

sam: taking ownership of postmortem. Initial RC hypothesis: runaway batch job worker retention + missing connection limits on frontends. Will coordinate with batch owners to patch and add rate limits.

alex: adding short-term alert tuning to reduce noise: set `maxclients` alert to warn earlier but only page on sustained 60s breach.

jia: logging notes for postmortem: collect `CLIENT LIST` snapshots, pgbouncer stats, LB conn metrics, and the batch job template that spawned workers.

ops-runner: making a ticket for permanent mitigations: connection limits in SDK, circuit-breaker on batch spawns, safe defaults for pgbouncer and redis configs. Ticket: RDW-INC-5992.

maya: status: service healthy, metrics stabilizing. closing PD escalation if no more bursts. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident RID-4281 status: RESOLVED by maya at 2188887968.

sam: will draft postmortem and proposed permanence changes. tagging product & infra.

alex: thumbs: :thumbsup: Good catch on the batch job. We'll follow up with a deploy to add per-worker connection caps and SDK idle-time pruning.

incident-bot: Runbook note appended: "Add step to check scheduled batch jobs and enforce per-worker connection caps".
